mainTopic: מרים's prophecy, יעקב's burial and עשו's challenge at the cave, and how משה recovered יוסף's bones.
overview: This amud finishes the story of מרים, who predicted the birth of ישראל's savior and stood by the river to see how her prophecy would end. The גמרא then explains the משנה's line 'יוסף זכה'. On the way to bury יעקב, the Egyptians at first did not honor his family. They changed once they saw thirty-six royal crowns hung on יעקב's coffin. At מערת המכפלה, עשו blocks the burial and claims the last grave. The brothers argue that he sold it, and they send נפתלי to Egypt for the bill of sale. Meanwhile חושים בן דן kills עשו, which fulfills רבקה's words about losing both sons on one day. The גמרא explains that the brothers let יוסף handle the burial because care from a king brings more honor. Next it praises משה, who went after יוסף's bones while everyone else took plunder. It gives two versions of how he found the casket: floating up from the נילוס, or shaking in the royal vault. The amud ends with passersby asking how a dead man's casket could travel beside the ארון of the שכינה, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: מרים's prophecy, its fulfillment, and her father's doubt
steps.stepSummary: מרים predicts the birth of a savior. When משה is born, the house fills with light and her father kisses her. When משה is thrown into the river, her father taps her head and asks where her prophecy went.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a child, מרים used to say: 'My mother is going to have a son who will save ישראל.' When משה was born, the whole house filled with light. Her father got up, kissed her on the head and said, 'My daughter, your prophecy came true.' But when they had to put משה into the river, her father got up, tapped her on the head and said, 'My daughter, where is your prophecy now?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story about מרים that started earlier. It shows her prophecy seeming to come true, and then seeming to fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two matching scenes. In the first, the light at משה's birth proves her prophecy, so her father kisses her. In the second, משה is put into the river and the prophecy looks broken, so her father taps her head in doubt. This sets up the next step, where a פסוק shows מרים waiting to see how things would end.

keyTerms.meaning: is going to, in the future (feminine)

phrases.english: And she would say: In the future my mother
phrases.notes: 'She' is מרים, as a young girl.

phrases.english: will give birth to a son who will save Israel.
And once Moses was born,
the entire house was filled with light.
Her father stood up and kissed her on her head,
he said to her: My daughter, your prophecy has been fulfilled.
And once they put him into the river,
her father stood up and tapped her on her head,
he said to her: My daughter, where is your prophecy?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹמֶרֶת: עֲתִידָה אִמִּי שֶׁתֵּלֵד בֵּן שֶׁמּוֹשִׁיעַ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier aggadah about מרים's prophecy, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מרים prophesied the birth of ישראל's savior. It seemed fulfilled at משה's birth and seemed to fail when he was put in the river.

steps.title: The פסוק shows מרים watching for how her prophecy would end
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'his sister stood far off, to know what would be done to him' is read as מרים waiting to see how her prophecy would turn out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that is what the פסוק means: 'His sister stood far away, to know what would be done to him.' She wanted to know how her prophecy would end up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the story to a פסוק in שמות. מרים stood by the river to see how her prophecy would play out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the פסוק says she wanted to see what would happen to the baby. The גמרא reads 'to know' as wanting to see the final outcome of her prophecy. That makes the story above the background to the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is what is written (connects a teaching to a פסוק)
at the end of, the outcome of

steps.whatToRemember: מרים stood by the river because she was waiting to see her prophecy come true, not just watching her baby brother.

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
"And his sister stood far off
phrases.notes: שמות 2:4

phrases.english: to know what would be done to him" —
to know what would be the outcome of her prophecy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the story in step 1 to a פסוק, closing the מרים section.
steps.raayaObject: That מרים was waiting to see whether her prophecy would come true.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 2:4: 'And his sister stood far off, to know what would be done to him.'

steps.title: Why the order of the burial procession changes
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה 'יוסף זכה', the גמרא asks why the Egyptians are listed before יוסף's brothers on the way up to bury יעקב, but after them on the way back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'יוסף merited...' The גמרא asks: Why does the תורה, at the beginning, write 'יוסף went up to bury his father, and all of פרעה's servants went up with him', and only afterward 'and all of יוסף's household, his brothers and his father's household'? And why, at the end, does it write 'יוסף returned to Egypt, he and his brothers', and only afterward 'and all who went up with him to bury his father'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, about יוסף burying יעקב. It points out a change in the order of the פסוקים and asks why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the trip up, פרעה's servants come before the brothers, which suggests the brothers were treated as less important. On the trip back, the brothers come right after יוסף and the Egyptians are mentioned last. The question is what happened in between to change the order.

phrases.english: Joseph merited, etc.
What is different at first, that it is written:
"And Joseph went up to bury his father
phrases.notes: בראשית 50:7

phrases.aramaic: וַיַּעֲלוּ אִתּוֹ כׇּל עַבְדֵי פַּרְעֹה וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, etc.",
and afterward: "And all the house of Joseph
and his brothers and his father's house",
and what is different at the end, that it is written:
"And Joseph returned to Egypt, he and his brothers",
and afterward: "and all who went up with him
to bury his father"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא מֵעִיקָּרָא דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, יוסף burying יעקב, after the מרים story ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוקים put the Egyptians first on the trip up but put the brothers first on the trip back.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the Egyptians honored them only after seeing their honor
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that at first the Egyptians did not show the family honor. After they saw how honored the family was, they began treating them with honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: At the beginning, before the Egyptians saw how honored ישראל were, they did not treat them with respect. At the end, after they saw it, they did treat them with respect.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question about the changing order. The Egyptians' attitude changed during the trip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of the list reflects how the Egyptians treated the brothers. On the way up they did not respect them, so they walked ahead. Something they saw along the way changed that, and the next step explains what it was.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
At first, before they saw
phrases.notes: 'They' means the Egyptians in the procession.

phrases.english: the honor of Israel —
they did not treat them with honor,
and in the end, once they saw their honor —
they treated them with honor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בַּתְּחִילָּה עַד שֶׁלֹּא רָאוּ בִּכְבוֹדָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Egyptians' respect changed once they saw the family's honor, so the order of the list changed with it.

steps.title: What was the honor? A question about 'גורן האטד'
steps.stepSummary: To show what honor the Egyptians saw, the גמרא quotes 'they came to גורן האטד' and asks how a thorn bush could have a threshing floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And they came to the threshing floor of the thorn bush.' But does a thorn bush have a threshing floor?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to show what honor the Egyptians saw. It quotes a פסוק with a strange phrase and asks what it means, which sets up רבי אבהו's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אטד' is a thorny bush. A threshing floor is where grain is processed, and nobody threshes thorns. The phrase looks odd, so it must be hinting at something, and that hint is the honor רבי יוחנן mentioned.

keyTerms.meaning: and is it so that...? (a question showing surprise)

phrases.english: As it is written: "And they came to the threshing floor of Atad",
phrases.notes: בראשית 50:10. The 'as it is written' explains what honor רבי יוחנן was talking about.

phrases.english: And does a thorn bush have a threshing floor?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי גוֹרֶן יֵשׁ לוֹ לָאָטָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up רבי יוחנן's answer by pointing to a פסוק, and raises a question about its wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What 'the threshing floor of the thorn bush' means, since thorns are not threshed.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: crowns around יעקב's coffin like thorns around a threshing floor
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that kings' crowns were placed around יעקב's coffin, the way a threshing floor is fenced with thorns. The children of עשו, ישמעאל and קטורה had all come.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: This teaches that they surrounded יעקב's coffin with crowns, the way a threshing floor is surrounded by a fence of thorn bushes. The descendants of עשו, ישמעאל and קטורה all came.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question about the strange phrase. It describes a ring of royal crowns around יעקב's coffin, and this is the honor that made the Egyptians respect the family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Threshing floors were fenced with thorny bushes to keep people out. In the same way, a circle of crowns surrounded the coffin. The kings who came from עשו, ישמעאל and קטורה honored יעקב, and the Egyptians saw it.
steps.whatToRemember: The order changed because the Egyptians saw kings honoring יעקב with crowns around his coffin. After that, they respected his family.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said: This teaches
that they surrounded Jacob's coffin with crowns
like this threshing floor that is surrounded with thorn bushes,
because the children of Esau came
and the children of Ishmael and the children of Keturah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהִקִּיפוּהוּ כְּתָרִים לַאֲרוֹנוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5 and completes the support for רבי יוחנן's answer in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'גורן האטד' describes royal crowns circling יעקב's coffin like thorns around a threshing floor. The crowns belonged to the kings descended from עשו, ישמעאל and קטורה.

steps.title: The kings came to fight but hung their crowns on יעקב's coffin
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the kings first came for war. When they saw יוסף's crown on יעקב's coffin, they hung their own crowns there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Sage taught: they all came to make war. Once they saw יוסף's crown hanging on יעקב's coffin, they all took their crowns and hung them on יעקב's coffin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that fills in the story behind רבי אבהו's crowns around the coffin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו said that crowns surrounded the coffin. This ברייתא explains how that happened: the kings arrived as enemies. Seeing יוסף's royal crown on the coffin turned them into honor-givers.

phrases.english: A Sage taught: they all came for war,
once they saw the crown of Joseph
hanging on the coffin of Jacob,
they all took their crowns
and hung them on the coffin of Jacob.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: כּוּלָּם לַמִּלְחָמָה בָּאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רבי אבהו's description of crowns around the coffin
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The kings came to fight, but they honored יעקב by hanging their crowns on his coffin after seeing יוסף's crown there.

steps.title: Thirty-six crowns hung on the coffin
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא gives the number: thirty-six crowns.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Sage taught: thirty-six crowns were hung on יעקב's coffin.
steps.whatsHappening: A second short ברייתא adds the number of crowns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows how great the honor was. It is the honor the Egyptians saw, which made them start treating the family with respect (step 4).

phrases.english: A Sage taught: thirty-six crowns
were hung on the coffin of Jacob.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: שְׁלֹשִׁים וְשִׁשָּׁה כְּתָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the number of crowns to the previous ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thirty-six crowns were hung on יעקב's coffin.
steps.whatToRemember: The Egyptians began honoring יעקב's family because they saw kings honoring him: thirty-six crowns on his coffin.

steps.title: Even the horses and donkeys mourned
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק about the 'very great and heavy' mourning, a ברייתא teaches that even the animals joined in.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And they mourned there a great and very heavy mourning." A Sage taught: even horses and even donkeys.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק in the funeral story and explains the extra words describing the mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק stacks up words: 'great' and 'very heavy.' The ברייתא reads this as mourning beyond the usual, so that even the animals took part.

phrases.english: "And they mourned there a great mourning,
phrases.notes: בראשית 50:10

phrases.english: and very heavy."
A Sage taught: even horses and even donkeys.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיִּסְפְּדוּ שָׁם מִסְפֵּד גָּדוֹל וְכָבֵד מְאֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with the next פסוק of the burial story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra wording in the פסוק teaches that even horses and donkeys mourned יעקב.

steps.title: עשו blocks the burial and claims the last grave
steps.stepSummary: At מערת המכפלה, עשו stops the burial. He argues that the cave holds only four couples, and since יעקב buried לאה in his own spot, the remaining spot belongs to עשו.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they reached מערת המכפלה, עשו came and blocked them. He said: "ממרא, קרית הארבע, which is חברון." רבי יצחק said that קרית ארבע means four couples: אדם and חוה, אברהם and שרה, יצחק and רבקה, יעקב and לאה. עשו argued: יעקב buried לאה in his own spot, so the spot that is left is mine.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves to the cave itself. עשו raises an objection to burying יעקב there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עשו builds his claim step by step. The name קרית ארבע shows there are only four spots for couples. יעקב already used his spot for לאה, so the one remaining spot must be עשו's.

keyTerms.meaning: The Cave of Machpelah, the burial cave of the אבות
"City of Four," another name for חברון
That remains or is left over

steps.confusionAlert: עשו is not saying יעקב has no right to the cave at all. He is saying יעקב already used up his own spot by burying לאה there, so the last spot is עשו's.

phrases.english: (From these, from these)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: Once they reached the Cave of Machpelah,
Esau came and was blocking them,
he said to them:
"Mamre, Kiryat Ha'arba, which is Hebron,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 35:27

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Kiryat Arba, because there were four couples:
Adam and Eve, Abraham and Sarah,
Isaac and Rebecca, Jacob and Leah.
He buried Leah in his own spot,
phrases.notes: "He" is יעקב. This is עשו talking now, not רבי יצחק.

phrases.english: and this one that is left over is mine.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִגִּיעוּ לִמְעָרַת הַמַּכְפֵּלָה, אֲתָא עֵשָׂו קָא מְעַכֵּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the story from the mourning to the dispute at the cave
steps.kashyaTarget: יעקב's right to be buried in מערת המכפלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The cave holds only four couples. יעקב already used his spot for לאה, so the last spot belongs to עשו.

steps.title: The brothers answer: you sold it
steps.stepSummary: יעקב's sons tell עשו that he sold his rights.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: You sold it.
steps.whatsHappening: The brothers give a short answer to עשו's claim: he no longer owns that spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They do not argue about how many spots there are. They argue that עשו gave up his rights when he sold to יעקב.

phrases.english: They said to him: You sold it.
phrases.notes: They mean the sale of the בכורה to יעקב for the lentil stew.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: זַבֵּינְתֵּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers עשו's claim
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies ownership: the rights were sold
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The last spot belongs to עשו
steps.terutzMaskana: עשו sold his rights to יעקב

steps.title: עשו: I sold the birthright, not my ordinary share
steps.stepSummary: עשו pushes back: he sold only the extra rights of the firstborn, not his basic share as a regular son.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Even if I sold the birthright, did I sell my plain share?
steps.whatsHappening: עשו challenges the brothers' answer by narrowing what the sale included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A firstborn gets extra rights, and every son also gets a regular share. עשו admits he sold the extra rights. He says his regular-son right to a grave was never part of the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: The plain, ordinary share of a regular son

phrases.english: He said to them:
Granted that I sold the birthright,
did I sell my ordinary share?

steps.triggerLanguage: נְהִי דְּזַבֵּינִי בְּכֵירוּתָא, פְּשִׁיטוּתָא מִי זַבֵּינִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the brothers' answer
steps.kashyaTarget: The brothers' claim that עשו sold his rights
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sale covered only the בכורה, not the regular share that would include a grave.

steps.title: Proof that עשו sold even his ordinary share
steps.stepSummary: The brothers say yes, he sold that too. They quote יעקב's words 'my grave that I כריתי for myself,' and רבי יוחנן explains that כירה means a sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Yes. As it is written: "In my grave that I כריתי for myself." רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: כירה means selling, because in the cities by the sea they call a sale כירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The brothers answer עשו's challenge with a פסוק and a word explanation showing that יעקב bought the grave itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעקב called the grave 'my grave that I כריתי.' Since כירה means buying or selling, the פסוק shows יעקב bought the burial spot. So even עשו's regular share in the cave was sold.

keyTerms.meaning: I dug, or here, I bought
A sale (in the language of overseas cities)
The cities by the sea, overseas

steps.whyThisMatters: The brothers' case rests on reading one word in a new way. This shows how a single word can settle an ownership dispute.

phrases.english: They said to him: Yes,
as it is written: "In my grave that I כריתי for myself,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 50:5. יוסף is quoting what יעקב told him.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:
"Kirah" is nothing other than a word for selling,
for in the cities by the sea
they call a sale "kirah."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: אִין, דִּכְתִיב: ״בְּקִבְרִי אֲשֶׁר כָּרִיתִי לִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers עשו's narrower claim with a פסוק
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a פסוק plus a word explanation
steps.terutzMaskana: יעקב bought the grave itself, so עשו's ordinary share was sold too
steps.raayaObject: That עשו sold even his ordinary share in the cave
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 50:5 "אשר כריתי לי," read as "which I bought," following רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק

steps.title: עשו demands the bill of sale
steps.stepSummary: עשו answers the brothers' claim by demanding written proof of the sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: עשו said to them: Show me the document!
steps.whatsHappening: עשו does not accept the brothers' word that he sold his share. He demands that they show him the written contract.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13 the brothers proved the sale from a פסוק. עשו now shifts the fight from 'did it happen?' to 'prove it with a document.' Without the paper in hand, the brothers cannot win on the spot.

keyTerms.meaning: a letter or document; here, the bill of sale

phrases.english: He said to them:
Bring me the document!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הַבוּ לִי אִיגַּרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: עשו pushes back on the brothers' claim from step 13 by demanding written proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: The brothers' claim that עשו sold his ordinary son's share too.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A spoken claim is not enough. Without the bill of sale, the claim is not proven.

steps.title: The document is in Egypt, so נפתלי is sent
steps.stepSummary: The brothers say the bill of sale is in מצרים and choose the swift נפתלי to go get it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: The document is in the land of Egypt. Who will go? נפתלי will go, because he is fast like a deer, as the פסוק says: 'נפתלי is a deer let loose, he gives beautiful words.'
steps.whatsHappening: The brothers admit the paper is not with them but say it exists in מצרים. They pick נפתלי, the fastest runner, to bring it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brothers do not give up their claim. They say the proof exists and is simply far away. Using יעקב's blessing that calls נפתלי a swift deer, they choose him as the messenger.

phrases.english: They said to him:
The document is in the land of Egypt.
And who will go?
Naphtali will go,
since he is swift like a doe,
as it is written:
"Naphtali is a doe let loose,
he gives goodly words."
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:21

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: אִיגַּרְתָּא בְּאַרְעָא דְמִצְרַיִם הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers עשו's demand for the document.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The proof exists but must be brought from far away.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the brothers cannot show a document, their claim fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: The document exists in מצרים, and the swift נפתלי will fetch it.

steps.title: רבי אבהו reads the verse as 'words of a document'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו rereads 'אמרי שפר' as 'אמרי ספר,' hinting at the document נפתלי went to bring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: Don't read it as 'beautiful words.' Read it as 'words of a document.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו shows that the same פסוק about נפתלי hints at this exact mission. He went to bring 'the words of a document.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the 'אל תקרי' style, which rereads one word with a similar sound: שפר becomes ספר. With that change, the blessing describes נפתלי as the runner who brought the bill of sale.

keyTerms.meaning: do not read it as (rereading a word to find a hint)
words of a document or book

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
Do not read "goodly words,"
but rather "words of a document."
phrases.notes: Swapping one similar-sounding letter turns "beautiful words" into "document words," a hint to the bill of sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: אַל תִּקְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a reading of the פסוק quoted in step 15 that ties it directly to the document.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words 'אמרי שפר' hint at 'אמרי ספר,' the document נפתלי brought.

steps.title: חושים learns why the burial is delayed
steps.stepSummary: חושים בן דן, who is hard of hearing, asks what is going on and is outraged that יעקב must wait unburied.
steps.simpleTranslation: חושים son of דן was there, and he was hard of hearing. He asked: What is going on? They told him: This man is holding us up until נפתלי comes back from מצרים. He said: Until נפתלי comes back from מצרים, should my grandfather lie here in disgrace?
steps.whatsHappening: The story brings in a new character, חושים. He did not hear the argument, so he asks what is happening. When he hears that the burial must wait, he protests. This sets up his action in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because חושים could not hear the legal back-and-forth, he sees only the plain result: יעקב is lying unburied. To him, leaving יעקב in disgrace while waiting for a document is unacceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: his ears were heavy, meaning he was hard of hearing

phrases.english: Hushim the son of Dan was there,
and his ears were heavy.
phrases.notes: He was hard of hearing, so he missed the whole argument.

phrases.english: He said to them: What is this?
And they said to him:
This one is holding things up
until Naphtali comes from the land of Egypt.
He said to them:
And until Naphtali comes from the land of Egypt,
shall my father's father lie in disgrace?

steps.triggerLanguage: חוּשִׁים בְּרֵיהּ דְּדָן תַּמָּן הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story while the brothers wait for נפתלי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חושים refuses to let יעקב lie unburied while the brothers wait for the document.

steps.title: חושים strikes עשו and יעקב smiles
steps.stepSummary: חושים kills עשו, עשו's eyes fall at יעקב's feet, and יעקב smiles, fulfilling a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He took a club and hit עשו on the head. עשו's eyes fell out and landed at יעקב's feet. יעקב opened his eyes and smiled. This is what the פסוק means: 'The righteous will rejoice when he sees revenge; he will wash his feet in the blood of the wicked.'
steps.whatsHappening: חושים ends the delay by force and kills עשו. The גמרא then connects the scene to a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is not settled with a document. It ends with עשו's death. The details, with eyes falling at יעקב's feet and יעקב smiling, match the פסוק about the righteous seeing revenge and 'washing his feet in the blood of the wicked.'

keyTerms.meaning: and this is what is written (showing a פסוק fits the event)

phrases.english: He took a club
and struck him on his head,
his eyes fell out
and fell at the feet of Jacob.
Jacob opened his eyes and smiled.
And this is what is written:
"The righteous shall rejoice when he sees vengeance;
he shall wash his feet in the blood of the wicked."
phrases.notes: תהלים 58:11

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁקַל קוּלְפָא מַחְיֵיהּ אַרֵישֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: חושים acts on the outrage he expressed in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עשו is killed at the cave, and the scene fulfills the פסוק 'ישמח צדיק כי חזה נקם.'

steps.title: רבקה's prophecy comes true
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this moment fulfilled רבקה's words about losing both sons on one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: At that moment רבקה's prophecy came true, as the פסוק says: 'Why should I lose both of you on one day?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps back from the story to point out that רבקה's words long ago were really a prophecy that came true at this moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Long before, רבקה worried she would lose both יעקב and עשו on the same day. The גמרא reads her words as a prophecy fulfilled when עשו died at יעקב's burial.

keyTerms.meaning: I will be bereaved, I will lose (my children)

phrases.english: At that moment
the prophecy of Rebecca was fulfilled,
as it is written:
"Why should I be bereaved of both of you in one day?"
phrases.notes: בראשית 27:45

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה נִתְקַיְּימָה נְבוּאָתָהּ שֶׁל רִבְקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the event of step 18 by linking it to רבקה's words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עשו's death on the day of יעקב's burial fulfilled רבקה's prophecy.

steps.title: Not the same day of death, but the same day of burial
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the prophecy came true through their burials, which were on one day, even though they died on different days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though they did not die on the same day, at least they were buried on the same day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא handles an obvious problem: יעקב and עשו did not die on the same day. It explains that the prophecy was fulfilled through their burials, which did fall on the same day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prophecy seems to be about death, but יעקב died earlier, in מצרים. The גמרא says 'one day' refers to their burial. עשו was killed and buried on the very day יעקב was buried.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא claims they died on the same day. It openly says they did not. Only the burials were on one day.

phrases.english: And even though their deaths
were not on one day,
their burials, at any rate,
were on one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּמִיתָתָן לֹא בְּיוֹם אֶחָד הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies how the prophecy in step 19 fits the facts.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the scope of the פסוק (burial, not death).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The prophecy should mean they died on the same day, which did not happen.
steps.terutzMaskana: The prophecy refers to their burial, which was on the same day.
steps.whatToRemember: The story of עשו at the cave ends with his death, and רבקה's prophecy is fulfilled through the shared day of burial.

steps.title: Why credit יוסף if the brothers were also involved?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to יוסף handling the burial. It asks whether the brothers would really have done nothing without him, since a פסוק shows they carried יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if יוסף had not taken care of יעקב, would his brothers not have taken care of him? But the פסוק says: 'His sons carried him to the land of כנען'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the story of עשו and returns to the earlier discussion of יוסף personally handling יעקב's burial. It challenges this with a פסוק showing that all the brothers were involved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the brothers carried יעקב to כנען, they were clearly ready to help. So why did יוסף have to handle the burial at the start? The question asks why the brothers stepped back.

keyTerms.meaning: dealt with him, took care of him
but isn't it written (a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: And if Joseph had not dealt with him,
phrases.notes: The extra אי in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: would his brothers not have dealt with him?
But isn't it written:
"And his sons carried him to the land of Canaan"?
phrases.notes: בראשית 50:13

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא אִיעֲסַק בֵּיהּ יוֹסֵף אֶחָיו לָא הֲווֹ מִעַסְּקִי בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the עשו story and returns to the earlier theme of יוסף's role in the burial.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's line 'יוסף זכה' (step 3), which implies that only יוסף took care of יעקב's burial, as if the brothers would not have done it without him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק shows the brothers carried יעקב, so they could have handled the burial themselves. Why did יוסף do it?

steps.title: More honor to be buried by a king
steps.stepSummary: The brothers let יוסף take care of it because it was a greater honor for יעקב to be handled by royalty than by ordinary people.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Let him do it. It is a greater honor for יעקב to be cared for by kings than by ordinary people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the brothers stepped back on purpose. They wanted יעקב to have the honor of being cared for by יוסף, who was a ruler.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brothers were willing to help, as the פסוק shows. They chose to give the job to יוסף for יעקב's honor. A burial handled by royalty brings the dead person more honor than one handled by common people.

keyTerms.meaning: leave it to him, let him do it

steps.whatToRemember: The brothers let יוסף handle יעקב's burial on purpose, because it was a greater honor for יעקב to be cared for by a king.

phrases.english: They said: Leave it to him,
his honor through kings is
greater than through ordinary people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: הַנִּיחוּ לוֹ, כְּבוֹדוֹ בִּמְלָכִים יוֹתֵר מִבְּהֶדְיוֹטוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the brothers' choice: a deliberate step back for the sake of honor.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The brothers could have handled the burial, so there was no reason for יוסף to do it.
steps.terutzMaskana: They left it to יוסף on purpose, because a king's care brings יעקב more honor.

steps.title: משה busied himself with מצוות while others took plunder
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about יוסף and brings a ברייתא praising משה for caring for יוסף's bones instead of collecting plunder.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Who is greater than יוסף,' etc. A ברייתא teaches: See how much משה loved מצוות. All of ישראל were busy taking the plunder of מצרים, but he was busy with a מצוה, as the פסוק says, 'The wise of heart will take מצוות.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא showing how much משה loved מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said יוסף was so great that משה himself took care of his bones. The ברייתא adds the contrast: everyone else was gathering gold and silver, while משה chose the מצוה. The פסוק in משלי is read as describing exactly this choice.

keyTerms.meaning: was busy with, occupied himself with

phrases.english: 'Who, to us, is greater than יוסף,' etc.
The Sages taught:
Come and see how beloved מצוות were
to משה our teacher,
for all of ישראל were busy with the plunder,
and he was busy with מצוות,
as it is said: 'The wise of heart will take מצוות,' etc.
phrases.notes: משלי 10:8

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָנוּ גָּדוֹל מִיּוֹסֵף כּוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the brothers burying יעקב to the next line of the משנה about יוסף's burial.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה showed his love of מצוות by caring for יוסף's bones while everyone else took plunder.

steps.title: How did משה know where יוסף was buried?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how משה could have known the location of יוסף's grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how did משה know where יוסף was buried?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question: how did משה find יוסף's grave? This sets up the story that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסף had died generations before משה, so his burial place was not something משה would simply know. The גמרא asks for the source of this knowledge, and the next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: and from where (how did he know)

phrases.english: And from where did משה our teacher know
where יוסף was buried?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the ברייתא by asking how משה could carry out this מצוה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of משה's knowledge of where יוסף was buried.

steps.title: סרח tells משה, and the casket floats up from the Nile
steps.stepSummary: סרח בת אשר tells משה that the casket was sunk in the נילוס. משה calls to יוסף at the river and the casket floats up.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: סרח בת אשר was still alive from that generation. משה went and asked her if she knew where יוסף was buried. She said: The Egyptians made him a metal casket and sank it in the נילוס so its waters would be blessed. משה stood at the river and called: 'יוסף, יוסף! The time has come that הקדוש ברוך הוא swore He would redeem you, and the time has come for the oath you made ישראל swear. If you show yourself, good; if not, we are free of your oath.' Right away יוסף's casket floated up.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: an old woman from יוסף's own generation told משה where the casket was, and משה called it up out of the river.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סרח lived long enough to bridge the generations, so she knew the secret. The Egyptians hid the casket in the river because they believed it would bless the water. משה tells יוסף that the redemption has arrived, so the oath to carry his bones out must now be kept, and the casket rises.

keyTerms.meaning: Serach, daughter of אשר, who lived from יעקב's generation until the Exodus

phrases.english: They said: סרח, the daughter of אשר,
remained from that generation.
משה went to her and said to her:

phrases.aramaic: כְּלוּם אַתְּ יוֹדַעַת הֵיכָן יוֹסֵף קָבוּר?
phrases.english: Do you know anything about where יוסף is buried?
She said to him: A metal casket
the Egyptians made for him
and they set it in the Nile river,
so that its waters would be blessed.

phrases.aramaic: הָלַךְ מֹשֶׁה וְעָמַד עַל שְׂפַת נִילוּס,
phrases.english: משה went and stood on the bank of the Nile,
and said to him: יוסף, יוסף!

phrases.aramaic: הִגִּיעַ הָעֵת שֶׁנִּשְׁבַּע הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: The time has come about which הקדוש ברוך הוא swore
'that I will redeem you,'
and the time has come for the oath you made ישראל swear.
phrases.notes: יוסף made them promise to carry his bones out of מצרים (בראשית 50:25).

phrases.english: If you show yourself, good;

phrases.aramaic: אִם לָאו — הֲרֵי אָנוּ מְנוּקִּין מִשְּׁבוּעָתֶךָ.
phrases.english: if not, we are free of your oath.
Immediately, יוסף's casket floated up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: סֶרַח בַּת אָשֵׁר נִשְׁתַּיְּירָה מֵאוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how משה knew where יוסף was buried.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סרח בת אשר told him the casket was in the נילוס, and it floated up when משה called to יוסף.

steps.title: Iron can float, as with אלישע's axe head
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא heads off the surprise that a metal casket could float by quoting the פסוק where אלישע made an iron axe head float.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't be amazed that iron could float, because it is written: 'As one man was cutting down a beam, the iron fell into the water... Alas, my master, it was borrowed! The man of God said: Where did it fall? He showed him the place, and he cut a stick and threw it there, and the iron floated.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא expects the learner to ask how a heavy metal casket could float, and brings a פסוק showing that iron floated before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story said the casket was metal, yet it floated, which goes against nature. The פסוק in מלכים shows that a נביא once made iron float. This sets up the קל וחומר in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: do not be amazed, do not wonder

phrases.english: And do not wonder how iron could float,
for it is written:
'And as one was felling a beam,
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 6:5–6

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת הַבַּרְזֶל נָפַל אֶל הַמָּיִם וְגוֹ׳
phrases.english: the iron fell into the water, etc.
Alas, my master, and it was borrowed!
And the man of God said: Where did it fall?
And he showed him the place,
and he cut a stick and threw it there,
and the iron floated.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַל תִּתְמַהּ הֵיאַךְ בַּרְזֶל צָף, שֶׁהֲרֵי כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim that the metal casket floated.
steps.raayaObject: That iron can float by a miracle.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב 6:5–6, where אלישע makes an iron axe head float.

steps.title: All the more so for משה
steps.stepSummary: A קל וחומר: if iron floated for אלישע, a student of a student of משה, it would surely float for משה himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And isn't this a קל וחומר? If for אלישע, the student of אליהו, who was the student of משה, iron floated, then for משה our teacher, all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof with a קל וחומר from the smaller person to the greater one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלישע is two levels below משה: he learned from אליהו, who learned the Torah of משה. If the student's student could make iron float, the teacher himself certainly could. So the floating casket is not surprising.

keyTerms.meaning: an argument from a lesser case to a greater one

steps.whatToRemember: The metal casket floating is a miracle, and it fits with the miracle of אלישע's floating iron, by a קל וחומר to משה.

phrases.english: And are these matters not a קל וחומר?
If אלישע, the student of אליהו,
and אליהו was the student of משה,
iron floated before him,
then before משה our teacher,
how much more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא דְּבָרִים קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the פסוק from the previous step to build a קל וחומר.
steps.raayaObject: That iron would certainly float for משה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from אלישע, who was a student of a student of משה.

steps.title: רבי נתן: יוסף was in the royal burial vault
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן gives a different location: יוסף was buried in the burial vault of the kings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: יוסף was buried in the burial vault of the kings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion about where יוסף was buried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the first version, which put the casket in the נילוס, רבי נתן says it was among the coffins of the Egyptian kings. That changes how משה would identify it, as the next step shows.

phrases.english: רבי נתן says:
He was buried in the burial vault of the kings.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: בְּקַבַּרְנִיט שֶׁל מְלָכִים הָיָה קָבוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the question of where יוסף was buried.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יוסף's casket was in the royal burial vault, not the נילוס.

steps.title: יוסף's casket shakes and משה takes it
steps.stepSummary: In רבי נתן's version, משה calls to יוסף at the royal vault, and יוסף's casket shakes so משה can take it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה went and stood at the royal burial vault and said: 'יוסף, the time has come that הקדוש ברוך הוא swore He would redeem you, and the time has come for the oath you made ישראל swear. If you show yourself, good; if not, we are free of your oath.' At that moment, יוסף's casket shook. משה took it and brought it to himself.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רבי נתן's version: משה says the same words as before, and this time the casket shakes instead of floating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's speech is almost word for word the same as in the first version. The difference is only the sign: among many royal coffins, יוסף's coffin shook, showing which one was his. Then משה took it.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree that משה called to יוסף with the same words and a miracle showed him the casket. They differ only on where it was (the נילוס or the royal vault) and what the sign was (floating or shaking).

phrases.english: משה went and stood
by the burial vault of the kings and said:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹסֵף, הִגִּיעַ עֵת שֶׁנִּשְׁבַּע הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: יוסף, the time has come about which הקדוש ברוך הוא swore
'that I will redeem you,'
and the time has come for the oath you made ישראל swear.
If you show yourself, good;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — הֲרֵי אָנוּ מְנוּקִּין מִשְּׁבוּעָתֶךָ.
phrases.english: and if not, we are free of your oath.

phrases.aramaic: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה נִזְדַּעְזַע אֲרוֹנוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף,
phrases.english: At that moment, יוסף's casket shook,
משה took it and brought it to himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָלַךְ מֹשֶׁה וְעָמַד עַל קַבַּרְנִיט שֶׁל מְלָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי נתן's version, matching the first version's speech but with a different sign.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At the royal vault, יוסף's casket shook when משה called, and משה took it.

steps.title: Two arks traveled side by side in the desert
steps.stepSummary: For all the years in the מדבר, יוסף's casket and the ארון of the שכינה traveled together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all those years that the Jewish people were in the desert, these two arks, one of a dead man and one of the Divine Presence, traveled together.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that יוסף's casket has been recovered, the גמרא describes what happened to it next. It traveled with the people right alongside the ארון of the שכינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא puts two very different objects side by side: a box holding a dead body and the holiest object in the camp. This strange pairing sets up the questions that come next.

keyTerms.meaning: Arks or boxes. Here it covers both a casket and the holy ארון.
A dead person. Here it means יוסף.

phrases.english: And all those years
that the Jewish people were in the desert,
these two arks were
one of a dead man
and one of the Divine Presence,
phrases.notes: This is the holy ארון of the covenant.

phrases.english: traveling together,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל אוֹתָן שָׁנִים שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמִּדְבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after משה has taken יוסף's casket.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יוסף's casket traveled together with the ארון of the שכינה throughout the years in the מדבר.

steps.title: Passersby ask what the two arks are
steps.stepSummary: People passing by ask what these two ארונות are.
steps.simpleTranslation: And passersby would say: What is the nature of these two arks?
steps.whatsHappening: Onlookers see two ארונות traveling together and ask what they are. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple request for information. The passersby do not yet know that one box holds a dead body.

keyTerms.meaning: Their nature, or what they are

phrases.english: and passersby would say:

phrases.aramaic: מָה טִיבָן שֶׁל שְׁנֵי אֲרוֹנוֹת הַלָּלוּ?
phrases.english: What is the nature of these two arks?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָיוּ עוֹבְרִין וְשָׁבִין אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the strange sight described in step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What are these two ארונות traveling together?

steps.title: One holds a dead man, one holds the Divine Presence
steps.stepSummary: They answer that one ארון is of a מת and the other is of the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: One is of a dead man and one is of the Divine Presence.
steps.whatsHappening: The people answer the passersby. One box holds a dead body and the other is the ארון of the שכינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer gives the passersby new information, and that information is exactly what bothers them. It leads straight into their challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: They said: One is of a dead man
and one is of the Divine Presence.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: אֶחָד שֶׁל מֵת וְאֶחָד שֶׁל שְׁכִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One ארון holds a dead man and the other is the ארון of the שכינה.

steps.title: How can a dead body travel with the Divine Presence?
steps.stepSummary: The passersby challenge how it is fitting for a מת to travel with the שכינה. The reply begins with "they said."
steps.simpleTranslation: And how is it the way of a dead man to travel with the Divine Presence? They said:
steps.whatsHappening: The passersby push back: a dead body next to the holy ארון seems improper. The step ends with "they said" as the reply begins, and that reply continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question is phrased as a question, but it works as a challenge. It assumes a dead body does not belong next to the שכינה. The answer will need to explain what made יוסף worthy of this.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it so...? It opens a question that pushes back.
Its way, or what is fitting for it

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not asking what the boxes are. That was already answered. It is objecting that this pairing seems wrong.

phrases.english: And how is it the way of a dead man
to travel with the Divine Presence?
They said:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מָה דַּרְכּוֹ שֶׁל מֵת לְהַלֵּךְ עִם שְׁכִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 32 and opens the reply.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that יוסף's casket travels next to the ארון of the שכינה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dead body seems out of place beside the holy ארון, so why would they be carried together?
